_README: Copy this file, rename it, and fill it in. This is the ONLY file you edit
to change what a video looks like or who is in it - no module needs
touching. Delete the _README and _hint keys when you are done; anything
starting with an underscore is ignored.
There is no sprite library. Every picture in a video is drawn from the
director's description of the line it illustrates, for that video, and is
not reused by the next one - reuse is what made every video look like the
last. So this file does not list poses or props: it says who exists and
what they look like, and the script decides the rest.
That draws one reference image per character - the only drawing that
outlives a video, and what stops a character drifting between shots.
A build draws any that are missing anyway; running it up front just gets
the wait out of the way.
Optional: add an entry to casts/styles.json (the art-style registry) to
give this style a display label or make it the default. Registering is
not required - a cast file in casts/ is discovered on its own.
Check it first:  python scripts/build.py --check  (validates the registry
name: my_cast
_hint_name: Lowercase, no spaces. Names the style's folder: casts/<name>/, which holds its character references.
description: One line on what this cast is for and who plays what.
style: REPLACE ME - the art direction, applied to every generated image
_hint_style: The single most important field. Name a specific, recognisable look and
the drawing technique, not a mood. Include line weight and shading.
Good:  'Studio Ghibli watercolour background art style, soft gouache
washes, visible paper grain, gentle outlines, muted palette'

background.prompt: REPLACE ME - the one plate every shot sits on

_hint_background: Worth more time than anything else here: the horizon decides whether
characters look planted or adrift. Say three things explicitly -
1. where the horizon sits ('low horizon two thirds down the frame')
2. that the middle is empty ('wide open empty middle with nothing in it')
3. that the edges stay clear (scenery 'only at the extreme left and
right edges', 'no taller than a quarter of the image')
Tall scenery at the edges frames the shot and makes every character look
small and lost. Ask for an empty stage, not a nice picture.

hero.role: what this character MEANS in the argument, not who they are
hero._hint_role: e.g. 'the boss and the capital', 'asks the naive question'. This is all the director is told about who is available, so say what they MEAN in the argument.
hero.look: REPLACE ME - the character's fixed appearance, in every drawing
_hint_look: The most important field about a character. It is what the reference
drawing is made from, and the reference is what every later drawing of
them is conditioned on. Be exhaustive and concrete: body shape, colours,
clothing, distinguishing features. Do not describe a pose or a mood -
the director writes those per shot.
_hint_relative_height: Height relative to the other characters, 0.3-3.0. Pick one character
as 1.0 and size the rest against them. The director sets one height
per shot and cannot keep the cast in proportion across shots; this
makes the relationship a fact of the cast instead.

_hint_look: Not a field in this file. Everything about how the finished video looks -
caption size and position, shot tightness, label colours, dissolve length,
layout clearance, matting strength - lives in casts/styles.json under
`look`, shared by every style. If THIS style needs to differ, add a
`look` block to its entry in casts/styles.json and write only the keys
that change; the rest is inherited.
